name: Engalm
kurzbeschreibung: The historic Engalm alpine hamlet at the Großer Ahornboden captivates with a traditional show dairy, centuries-old sycamore maples, and Karwendel cliffs.
preis: Alpine village and natural monument freely accessible; toll road Hinterriß-Eng applies (cars approx. €5.50)
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily from mid-May to late October (closed in winter)
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied and scenic Engalm sits at 1,227 meters above sea level in the heart of the Karwendel mountains, forming the dramatic cul-de-sac of the Rißtal valley. Flanked by sheer limestone ramparts of the Hinterautal-Vomper Chain, this alpine hamlet is nestled within the world-famous natural monument of the Großer Ahornboden. Across a vast, lush valley floor grow over two thousand ancient sycamore maple trees, many between 300 and 600 years old, which blaze in brilliant golden yellow every autumn. Engalm is the oldest documented alpine hamlet in Tyrol, looking back on more than a thousand years of continuous pastoral history. The picturesque ensemble of timber chalets, sun-baked barns, and a rustic chapel operates each summer as a cooperative alpine dairy farm where around five hundred dairy cows graze on nutrient-rich pastures.

Route & Requirements

The grounds of Engalm are conveniently reached from the large visitor car park via an entirely level, barrier-free gravel trail in just ten minutes. This short interpretive path accommodates wheelchairs and pushchairs easily and leads directly through ancient maple groves into the heart of the village. For mountain hikers, the Eng is a springboard for high-alpine adventures: popular routes lead over the Hohljoch to the Falkenhütte (approx. 2.5 hours walking, 600 vertical meters, moderate) or up to the Lamsenjochhütte beneath the striking Lamsenspitze. These trails demand surefootedness, head for heights, and ankle-high mountain boots with deep tread. Families love the interactive nature trail and the spacious alpine adventure playground beside the main inn.

Visit & Arrival

Engalm and the Großer Ahornboden are open daily during the snow-free summer season from mid-May to late October. Access by car is solely via Bavarian territory from Lenggries through Vorderriß to Hinterriß; from Hinterriß, a private toll road (toll approx. €5.50 per car) runs 12 kilometers to the village. Public transport options include the Karwendel mountain bus (RVO line 9569), running several times daily from Lenggries and Bad Tölz straight to Engalm.

Tips

Do not miss visiting the historical show dairy at Engalm, where award-winning alpine cheese and fragrant butter are crafted daily over traditional copper vats. Stop at the shady beer garden to sample fresh Kaiserschmarrn served with apple compote.
